market_context: United States; home freezing of shell eggs and egg components
title: Can you freeze eggs?

seo.title: Can you freeze eggs?
seo.meta_description: Yes, but not in the shell. Whole beaten eggs, whites and properly prepared yolks can be frozen. USDA recommends about 12 months for best quality.
seo.search_intent: Find out which parts of an egg can be frozen, why shell eggs should not be frozen and how to freeze whole eggs, whites and yolks.

excerpt: Yes, but remove the shell first. USDA advises against freezing raw eggs in their shells because expansion can crack them. Whole eggs can be beaten and frozen, whites freeze very well, and yolks need a small amount of salt or sugar to reduce thickening and gelation. For best quality, USDA recommends using frozen blended eggs, whites or yolks within about 12 months.
content_html:
If a carton of eggs is not going to be used in time, the freezer can help—but not with the eggs still in their shells. Raw eggs can be frozen after they are removed from the shell; shell eggs should not be intentionally frozen because the contents expand and can crack the shell.

What parts of an egg freeze well?

ProductFreezer?USDA best-quality reference
Raw whole egg, out of shell and beatenYesUp to 12 months
Raw egg whitesYes, very wellUp to 12 months
Raw egg yolksYes, with preparationUp to 12 months
Raw egg in shellDo not intentionally freeze—
Hard-cooked eggPoor quality after freezing—

A freezer kept at 0 °F (−18 °C) or below preserves frozen food safely for longer; the 12-month recommendation is primarily about quality. Texture and flavor can decline with extended storage.

How to freeze whole eggs

Crack the eggs into a clean bowl, remove any shell fragments and beat yolks and whites together until blended. There is no need to whip in lots of air. Portion the mixture into small freezer-safe containers or food-safe ice trays if measured amounts will be useful later.

Label the package with the date and number of eggs. That small step prevents having to guess how many eggs a frozen block represents when you use it in a recipe.

Egg whites are the easiest

USDA notes that whites freeze very well and can even be whipped into meringue after proper thawing. Freeze them individually or in measured quantities in a clean, closed container.

If you freeze individual portions in a tray, transfer the solid cubes to a sealed freezer bag or container afterward to reduce drying and odor pickup.

Yolks need one extra step

An untreated yolk tends to become thick and syrupy or gel-like when frozen, making it difficult to blend smoothly after thawing. USDA recommends slightly modifying the yolks before freezing to limit that texture change.

For 4 yolks, USDA's method is a pinch of salt if they will be used in savory food, or approximately 1½ teaspoons sugar or corn syrup for sweet recipes. Label which ingredient was added so a salted yolk does not end up in dessert by surprise.

What if shell eggs freeze accidentally?

If an egg cracks during freezing, USDA recommends discarding it. A broken shell no longer provides an intact barrier around the contents.

If the shell remains uncracked, USDA advises keeping the egg frozen until needed and then thawing it in the refrigerator. It can be hard-cooked successfully, although the yolk may have thickened enough to limit other uses.

How to thaw frozen eggs

Move them to the refrigerator and let them thaw under refrigeration. Do not leave raw egg thawing on the counter for hours. Once thawed, use it in a preparation that will be cooked appropriately.

Pre-measured frozen portions are especially useful for baking and cooking. Repeated freezing and thawing is best avoided because each cycle can further damage texture.

Hard-cooked eggs are different

USDA does not recommend freezing hard-cooked eggs for quality. The white can become tough, watery or rubbery after thawing. Refrigerated hard-cooked eggs have a reference storage time of about 1 week.

Cooked dishes that contain eggs, such as some casseroles and quiches, may freeze more successfully than a hard-cooked egg by itself; texture depends on the other ingredients.

The practical rule

Freeze the egg contents, not the shell. Whole beaten eggs and whites can go into the freezer directly; yolks benefit from salt or sugar to protect texture. Label the portions and use 12 months as the best-quality window.

faq.question: Can you freeze a whole egg in its shell?
faq.answer: Do not intentionally do so. The contents expand and may crack the shell. Crack the egg and blend the yolk and white before freezing instead.

faq.question: How long do frozen eggs last?
faq.answer: USDA recommends using frozen blended whole eggs, whites or yolks within about 12 months for best quality.

faq.question: How do you freeze egg yolks?
faq.answer: USDA recommends mixing four yolks with a pinch of salt for savory use or 1½ teaspoons sugar or corn syrup for sweet use to limit thickening during freezing.

faq.question: Can hard-boiled eggs be frozen?
faq.answer: They do not freeze well. The whites undergo major texture changes; USDA recommends keeping hard-cooked eggs refrigerated for up to one week instead.
